The stock trades toward cash plus a small option; the market keeps some scarcity premium, so ~$50.

base.story: Fundamental value ~$54.6 (engine base). Execution is on track (first Oak Ridge centrifuge, CFC package, capex ~$700M in 2027) but contract pricing stays undisclosed and the trading book shrinks into 2028. The scarcity premium the market pays for the only US-owned enricher erodes only partly over 12 months, so ~$95.

bull.story: Fundamental value ~$93 (engine bull) plus the strategic premium coming back: large prepaid offtakes, a further DOE LEU or HALEU award, phase 2 sanctioned, SWU term price above $220, nuclear sentiment recovers with lower yields; the first warrant series ($226.86) comes into view.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: There is no listed pure-play enrichment peer (Urenco, Orano and Rosatom are state or privately held), so fewer than 10 genuine comparables exist. The discount reflects the finite life of the core earnings: the TENEX contract ends in 2028, Import Ban waivers end in 2027 and Orano supply ends in 2030 (10-K/10-Q), so trailing EBITDA has no terminal value like BWXT's naval-reactor franchise or CEG's fleet. The expansion is valued separately by rNPV, not by a multiple.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$40 the market would price Centrus below my cash floor plus core (~$35/share at the horizon, ~$45 today), i.e. as if the expansion is likely abandoned or must be refinanced with heavy dilution. That would most likely mean something fundamental broke: a capex blow-out or schedule reset past 2031, loss or delay of DOE milestone funding, or TENEX deliveries stopping with customer penalties. It would not be ordinary volatility.

reverse_dcf_check: At $109.88 the market pays ~$1.32B for core plus expansion after net cash, Westerman and the convert discount, against my ~$0.25B. It needs the Piketon build-out at roughly my bull case (~$800M peak revenue, 52% margin, 85% success, ~$2.0B capex). The engine says the multiples imply a 6.6% WACC versus 9.9%. The 6x horizon multiple on the core assumes its EBITDA declines toward zero after 2030, while the engine's fade (to 3% growth by year 10, margins held) is, if anything, generous to a book whose supply contracts end.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT after SBC (FY2025 $5.7M, F43; 2026 elevated by the $17.2M Q2 RSU tax-withholding charge and the Aug-2026 special Performance RSUs that vest on first-cascade enrichment). The share count grows only for expected equity raises and residual RSU settlement, so SBC is counted once.

reasoning: Primary-document lane. The 10-K/10-Q show that the profitable part of Centrus today, a trading book reselling TENEX/Orano SWU bought at 2018-reset prices, is finite. Waivers end in 2027, TENEX in 2028 and Orano in 2030, and firm LEU RPO is only ~$0.7B to 2030. Value therefore rests on the Piketon build-out: 12 t/yr HALEU plus LEU for the $2.4B definitive backlog, first output 2029, a 'multi-billion' cost, prices and margins under NDA. Cash after the September raise (~$2.1B, ~$0.9B net of converts at face) is real, but ~$0.74B of it is spent by the horizon. A milestone rNPV with explicit abandonment shows the initial build-out roughly NPV-neutral to modestly positive at a 10% rate: $2.85B capex, $900M DOE milestones, $600M peak revenue at 45% margin. A phase-2 option adds ~$7/share. Engine fair value $54.56; a haircut General Matter private mark (~$113) is the high leg, the cash floor (~$35) the low one. The reverse DCF shows the market pricing roughly my bull case. For the traded-price ladder I do not assume convergence to fair value within 12 months. The stock is a sentiment and rates proxy (-71% in a year, 89% vol, ~30% short), and the scarcity premium for the only US-owned enricher is durable, so the scenarios blend fundamental value with that premium persisting: bear $50 (30%), base $95 (50%), bull $190 (20%), each lognormal with 35% within-scenario vol. That gives a median ~$88, mean ~$103 and P(>=$110) ~0.36. Research was limited: the Bigdata.com credits were used up, Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage consensus were unavailable, and the IR site and Benzinga/Axios were blocked. Call content comes from the Motley Fool transcripts and summaries.

model_inputs.structure_note: The standard structure cannot describe a business whose value is a 2029+ enrichment plant still being built, so: the years hold only the core (TENEX/Orano-supplied LEU trading book + Technical Solutions, ex expansion costs), which is finite-life (TENEX 2028, Orano 2030) and fades from FY2028; the Piketon initial build-out and a phase-2 option are an rnpv adjustment (milestone phases, dated capex as probability-weighted dev costs, DOE milestones as milestones_pv); Westerman and the 0% convert discount are equity adjustments; pre-horizon capital deployment is in net_debt_horizon. Custom legs carry the brief's methods: (a)+(e) cash floor plus milestone option tree with abandonment (0.35 set, 0.42 after the engine normalises) and (f) a haircut private-round mark (0.10 set, 0.12 effective); EV/EBITDA is a 0.05 (0.06 effective) cross-check.
